proposals.evidence: Turner gives Prakrit puccha/puṃcha, Hindi pū̃ch, Kumaoni pūch and Gujarati pũch tail, with feminine pūchī and an expanded MIA *puṃchiā explicitly discussed in the article. These survey puc-/pũc- tail forms belong to that documented family with ordinary final-vowel variation. Nasalized forms are covered by the article’s puñcha addendum; expanded ṛ/ḍ or l stems are not collapsed into this plain branch.
